references.text: The Lord is your life and the length of your days. Both texts connect God's word to life itself and to living long in the land.
Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that goes out from the mouth of the Lord. Both texts emphasize that God's word is the source of life.
The one who keeps the Lord's commands shall live by them. A common theme that obedience to God's word gives life.
Proverbs describes wisdom and God's word as life for those who find them, parallel to how God's word is life for Israel.
Keeping the Lord's commands leads to prosperity for the people and allows them to live long in the land. The same promise of a long life in the land.
Obedience to God's word gives many days in the land that the Lord swore to give the fathers. A common theme about inheriting the land and living long.
Jesus says that his words are spirit and life. The New Testament confirms that God's word gives life.
Peter confesses that Jesus has the words of eternal life. Parallel to how God's word is life itself.
Paul holds forth the word of life. God's word as a source of life is a recurring theme.
God's word is living and active. Both texts emphasize the life-giving power of God's word.
